Reading a fit, for packages that extend flexyBayes

Source: R/extension_api.R, R/fixed_design.R
fb_extension.Rd

A package built on flexyBayes reads a fitted model through these functions, fb_refit(), fb_marginal_cov(), fb_isolated_lapply() and the refusal registry (fb_register_refusals(), fb_refuse()), and never through the package's internal functions. fb_extension_api() gives the version of that set. A package checks it in its .onLoad() and refuses to load against a version it was not written for.

Builds the fixed-effect design matrix of formula over data, as flexyBayes builds it for its aliasing check, with the term of each column and the order in which ASReml 4.2 enters the columns.

Usage

fb_extension_api()

fb_model_terms(fit)

fb_response_values(response, data)

fb_offset_values(offsets, data, newdata = FALSE)

fb_model_weights(terms)

fb_known_variance(terms)

fb_engine_settings(engine)

fb_convergence(fit)

fb_inla_posterior_sample(fit, n, ...)

fb_check_refit(fit, caller = "")

fb_fixed_design(formula, data, train_rows = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A flexyBayes fit.

response

The response as written in the model: a column name or an R expression in the columns of data.

data

A data frame.

offsets

The offset terms of a model as written, for example "offset(log(area))", fb_model_terms(fit)$offsets.

newdata

TRUE when data holds new rows for a prediction, so that a missing offset column is refused with a message that says so.

terms

A model description from fb_model_terms(), or a fit.

engine

NULL, an fb_engine object, or a named list of sampler settings.

n

The number of posterior samples.

...

Further arguments to INLA::inla.posterior.sample(), for example seed, num.threads or selection.

caller

Text placed in front of a refusal's message, naming the function that asked.

formula

A one-sided formula of fixed terms.

train_rows

Row numbers of the training rows, or NULL (default) to learn transforms from every row.

Value

  • fb_extension_api(): an integer, the version of the set. It is 1.

  • fb_model_terms(): a list, or NULL for an object that carries none.

  • fb_response_values(): a vector with one value per row of data, or NULL when the response cannot be evaluated there.

  • fb_offset_values(): a numeric vector with one value per row of data, or NULL when the model has no offset.

  • fb_model_weights(): the numeric weights, or NULL for an unweighted model.

  • fb_known_variance(): NULL for a model without a known variance. Otherwise a list with values (one variance per row of the fitted data), matrix (the known covariance, or NULL for a vector), column (the data column that carries each row's variance) and inla_index (the index of the row effect that carries it in an INLA formula).

  • fb_engine_settings(): a named list, empty for NULL.

  • fb_convergence(): a list with engine, ok (TRUE, FALSE or NA), reasons and evidence.

  • fb_inla_posterior_sample(): the list INLA::inla.posterior.sample() returns, with the linear predictor and the hyperparameters on the scale of the data.

  • fb_check_refit(): fit, invisibly.

A list: X (the matrix), terms, frame (the model frame), xlev (the factor levels), assign (the term index of each column), column_terms (the term label of each column) and asreml_order (the column positions in ASReml's order: term by term, and within a term by descending factor levels with the first factor varying slowest).

Details

  • fb_model_terms() returns the model description of a fit: the parsed fixed, random, residual and addition terms, the response, the family and the link, as the engines received them.

  • fb_response_values() evaluates a response, a column name or an expression such as "log(y)", over data.

  • fb_offset_values() sums the offsets of a model over the rows of data, refusing an offset that is not a finite number on every row.

  • fb_model_weights() returns the observation weights a model was fitted with.

  • fb_known_variance() describes the known variance or covariance of a model and where it is carried in the data.

  • fb_engine_settings() checks and returns sampler settings.

  • fb_convergence() returns the convergence verdict that summary(fit) reports, with its evidence.

  • fb_inla_posterior_sample() draws joint posterior samples of an INLA fit on the scale of the data.

  • fb_check_refit() refuses a fit that cannot be refitted as the model it was fitted as.

  • fb_fixed_design() builds the design matrix of a fixed formula.

Factor levels and contrasts are those of all of data. With train_rows, a transform that learns from the rows it is evaluated on (scale(), poly(), splines::ns(), splines::bs()) learns from the training rows alone and is applied with those parameters to every row, the rule of stats::predict(). Missing values are kept as rows of NA.

Examples

fb_extension_api()
#> [1] 1
d <- data.frame(y = c(1, 4, 9), area = c(1, 2, 3))
fb_response_values("sqrt(y)", d)
#> [1] 1 2 3
fb_offset_values("offset(log(area))", d)
#> [1] 0.0000000 0.6931472 1.0986123
fb_engine_settings(list(chains = 2L))
#> $chains
#> [1] 2
#> 
fb_fixed_design(~ area, d)$X
#>   (Intercept) area
#> 1           1    1
#> 2           1    2
#> 3           1    3
#> attr(,"assign")
#> [1] 0 1
